discovery: Quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion: cavity optomechanics and the quantum ground state of engineered mechanical oscillators

nominees.name: Tobias J. Kippenberg
nominees.affiliation: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland

subfield: Quantum optics / hybrid quantum systems (optomechanics and electromechanics)
motivation: The nominees showed that the motion of engineered mechanical objects, containing billions of atoms, obeys quantum mechanics and can be controlled. Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer established cavity optomechanics, demonstrating radiation-pressure sideband cooling, strong optomechanical coupling and quantum-limited measurement of mechanical motion. Cleland, coupling a superconducting qubit to a piezoelectric resonator (2010), brought a mechanical oscillator to its quantum ground state and created and controlled its single phonon states for the first time. Together these advances opened a new regime of macroscopic quantum physics. Now that the 2025 prize recognised quantum effects in electrical circuits, this is the natural next step: quantum mechanics in mechanical motion. The work enables tests of quantum mechanics at large mass scales, quantum-limited force and displacement sensing relevant to gravitational-wave detection, and microwave-to-optical transducers, which are essential for networking superconducting quantum processors.
